cypher:
MATCH (n) WHERE n.dataset=$dataset AND n.repo=$repo AND n.id IN $evidence_ids
RETURN n.id AS evidence_id,n.label AS kind,n.path AS path,n.sha AS commit,n.number AS number,
n.title AS title,n.email AS email,n.login AS login,n.name AS name,
substring(coalesce(n.content,n.body,n.message,''),0,2400) AS excerpt ORDER BY evidence_id

rows.title: Make the openmrs-api surefire crash on 2.8.x explain itself
rows.excerpt:
## Description of what I changed

Since 24 July the `openmrs-api` surefire fork has been aborting with `SIGABRT` (`Process Exit Code: 134`, `Aborted (core dumped)`) partway through the suite on 2.8.x, failing nearly every pull request against the branch (#6394, #6262, #6230, #6219 and the last two pushes to 2.8.x itself). Contributors have started pushing empty "re-run CI" commits to get around it.

Every test that ran passed, so the console log had nothing to point at:

```
[INFO] Running org.openmrs.liquibase.ChangeLogDetectiveTest
Aborted (core dumped)
[WARNING] Tests run: 1765, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 23
[WARNING] Corrupted channel by directly writing to native stream in forked JVM 1. See ... the dump file ....dumpstream
[ERROR] The forked VM terminated without properly saying goodbye. VM crash or System.exit called?
```

That "corrupted channel" warning is the JVM writing its own explanation for the abort to stdout. Surefire diverts it into a `.dumpstream` file instead of the console, and the runner is torn down before anyone can read it, so the one piece of evidence that identifies the cause was being discarded on every failure.

This PR keeps that evidence: on a failed build it prints the surefire dump files and any `hs_err_pid*.log` into the job log, uploads them with `target/surefire-reports` as a per-job artifact, and reports free disk and memory. It also sets `fail-fast: false`, because the first crashing job was cancelling the other four, so a red build could not show whether a crash was specific to one Java version.

Nothing here changes what gets built or tested; it is all gated on `if: failure()`.

## What the first run found

It worked, and the crash is no longer a mystery. **These are two different JVM bugs, not a test failure.**

`build (ubuntu-latest, 11)`, Temurin 11.0.31+11:

```
#  Internal Error (moduleEntry.cpp:263), pid=2394, tid=2395
#  guarantee(java_lang_Module::is_instance(module)) failed: The unnamed module for ClassLoader
#  jdk.internal.reflect.DelegatingClassLoader, is null or not an instance of java.lang.Module.
#  The class loader has not been initialized correctly.
```

with the crash reached through reflection accessor generation from Mockito's inline mock maker:

```
V  [libjvm.so+0xc1828a]  ModuleEntry::create_unnamed_module(ClassLoaderData*)+0xca
V  [libjvm.so+0xf139db]  Unsafe_DefineClass0+0x37b
J  jdk.intern

rows.title: TRUNK-6512: Introduce ConceptReferenceRangeContext API
rows.excerpt:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **dkayiwa** · [Slack thread](https://openmrs.slack.com/archives/C021QUDSD5K/p1788308814384069)_

## Description of what I changed

This is a backport of TRUNK-6512 to the `2.7.x` maintenance branch. It is ported from the current state of `2.8.x` rather than cherry-picked from the original 2.7.x commit, because that commit (`f127132c`) was written against the old Velocity-based criteria utility, which TRUNK-6610 has since replaced with SpEL on this branch.

**Before:** resolving a concept reference range on 2.7.x means going through an `Obs`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` fabricates a throwaway `new Obs(person, concept, null, null)` and hands it to `new ObsValidator().getReferenceRange(obs)`, and the whole selection algorithm — evaluating each range's criteria, falling back to the `ConceptNumeric`'s own bounds, and merging multiple matches into the strictest range — lives inside the validator. A caller that only has a person and a concept, or that wants ranges evaluated as of some date other than today (retrospective data entry, for instance), has no way to say so: the criteria are always evaluated against a synthetic Obs with a null `obsDatetime`.

**After:** there is a first-class `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` that carries the person, the concept, an optional evaluation date, and — when it was built from one — the originating `Obs` and `Encounter`. `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange(ConceptReferenceRangeContext)` resolves a range from that context, and the selection algorithm now lives in `ConceptServiceImpl` where the rest of the concept logic is, instead of in a validator. Criteria expressions can use `$context` alongside the existing `$patient`, `$obs`, `$encounter`, `$date`, and `$fn`, and `$date` now reflects the context's date rather than always coming from an Obs.

## How

- New `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/ConceptReferenceRangeContext.java`, with constructors for `(Person, Concept, Date)`, `(Obs)`, and `(Encounter, Concept)`.
- `ConceptService`/`ConceptServiceImpl` gain the `ConceptReferenceRangeContext` overload; `ConceptReferenceRangeUtility` gains `evaluateCriteria(String, ConceptReferenceRangeContext)`.
- The existing `evaluateCriteria(String, Obs)` and `getConceptReferenceRange(Person, Concept)` signatures are kept and now delegate to the context-based versions,
